g.text: Adding robots stops buying throughput, and the planners give up at different points

text.style: font-size: 8.5px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans', sans-serif; fill: #52514e

g.text: Taller is better; the x axis is how many robots share the floor. Every line rises and then falls: past some density the robots spend their

text.style: font-size: 8.5px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans', sans-serif; fill: #52514e

g.text: time getting out of each other's way. Where a line turns over is the honest characterisation of a planner, and it is the thing a single bar

text.style: font-size: 8.5px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans', sans-serif; fill: #52514e

g.text: cannot show. At 5 robots on `corridors` the leader is Token Passing, not aisleflow. Token Passing then falls away as the floor fills, which is what its own completeness proof predicts:

text.style: font-size: 8.5px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans', sans-serif; fill: #52514e

g.text: it assumes every agent has a parking endpoint to rest at, and a crowded warehouse is exactly where that assumption runs out. Plain lifelong PIBT

text.style: font-size: 8.5px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans', sans-serif; fill: #52514e

g.text: is not plotted here -- it is this planner with its mechanisms off, and it belongs to the ablation ladder, which is the next figure.

text.style: font-size: 7px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans', sans-serif; text-anchor: start; fill: #898781
